steps.label: Calcium score
steps.detail: If a non-contrast scan was acquired, record the total and per-vessel Agatston scores.
steps.look: Non-contrast ECG-triggered images; confirm that each calcified focus is assigned to the correct vessel before accepting the total.
steps.normal: CAC: total 0 Agatston units (LM 0 | LAD 0 | LCx 0 | RCA 0). A zero CAC score does not exclude non-calcified plaque.
findings: CAC: total ___ Agatston units (LM ___ | LAD ___ | LCx ___ | RCA ___).
CAC: not performed.
steps.tip: Agatston scoring is defined on the non-contrast acquisition; do not derive it from contrast-enhanced images.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces provide orientation only. They do not depict calcific foci or permit Agatston scoring; use the acquired non-contrast CT.

steps.label: Dominance and anatomy
steps.detail: Establish dominance, origins, proximal course and coronary anomalies.
steps.look: Axial source images and volume rendering at the sinuses of Valsalva; follow each ostium and its proximal course relative to the aorta and pulmonary trunk; find which artery supplies the PDA.

normal.CORONARY ORIGINS / COURSE: Normal origins of the left main and right coronary arteries from the left and right coronary sinuses, with a normal proximal course. No myocardial bridge or fistula.

findings: Anomalous origin of the [RCA / LCA] from the [opposite / non-coronary] sinus with an [interarterial / retroaortic / prepulmonic / septal] course.
High-risk anomaly features: [slit-like ostium / acute take-off / intramural segment / proximal narrowing].
Myocardial bridge of the [mid LAD], __ mm long and __ mm deep.
Coronary artery fistula from the [ ] to the [ ].
steps.tip: Name an interarterial course between the aorta and pulmonary trunk explicitly, with any intramural segment or slit-like ostium.
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross left/right coronary trunks, LAD, circumflex and an RCA-derived posterior branch are available. Individual ostia, sinus anatomy, branch origins and anomalous courses are not independently resolved. Determine patient dominance from the images; do not assume the example circulation.

steps.label: Stenosis by segment
steps.detail: Record vessel and segment, plaque composition and the highest confident stenosis category.
steps.look: Curved MPR along each vessel, then orthogonal cross-sections at the tightest point and at a normal reference segment; check the axial source images for artefact.

normal.CORONARY FINDINGS: LM, LAD and diagonal branches, LCx and obtuse marginal branches, and RCA/PDA/PLV: no plaque or stenosis.

findings: [Vessel/segment]: [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque with [minimal 1–24% / mild 25–49% / moderate 50–69% / severe 70–99%] stenosis; series __ image __.
[Vessel/segment]: total occlusion, __ mm long, [with / without] distal reconstitution.
[Segment] non-diagnostic because of [motion / blooming calcification / poor opacification]; significant stenosis cannot be excluded.
steps.tip: Blooming from dense calcification overestimates stenosis; grade on orthogonal cross-sections with a wide window.
steps.anatomy_note: Gross artery surfaces do not establish the lumen, reference diameter, individual branch segments, plaque or stenosis. Use acquired orthogonal CT lumen sections and document non-evaluable segments.

steps.label: Plaque and burden
steps.detail: Describe plaque type and high-risk features, then state burden with the method used; no plaque is not P1.
steps.look: Cross-sections through each plaque for attenuation, remodelling and spotty calcification; count plaque-containing segments for SIS, or use the CAC score.

normal.PLAQUE BURDEN: No plaque; no plaque-burden category is assigned.

findings: High-risk plaque in the [segment]: [positive remodelling / low attenuation / spotty calcification / napkin-ring sign]; at least two features are present, so the HRP modifier applies.
Predominantly [calcified / non-calcified / partially calcified] plaque in __ segments.
Segment involvement score __ ([method]); overall plaque burden P__.
steps.tip: HRP needs at least two high-risk features within the same plaque.
steps.anatomy_note: No plaque geometry, calcific distribution or high-risk plaque morphology is represented in this atlas. Normal surface meshes cannot prove absence of plaque or its burden.

steps.label: Stents, grafts and physiology
steps.detail: Assess stent and graft patency, and record CT-FFR or perfusion when available.
steps.look: Sharp-kernel reconstructions with a wide window for the stent lumen; follow each graft from origin through its body to the distal anastomosis and run-off.

normal.STENTS / GRAFTS: No coronary stents or bypass grafts.

findings: Stent in the [vessel/segment]: [patent / in-stent restenosis __% / occluded / non-diagnostic].
[LIMA / RIMA / SVG] to [target]: [patent / stenosis at __ / occluded]; distal anastomosis [ ].
CT-FFR __ measured 1–2 cm distal to the [segment] lesion; lowest distal value __ in [vessel].
steps.tip: Report the lesion-specific CT-FFR value 1–2 cm beyond the lesion, separately from the lowest distal value.
steps.anatomy_note: Stents, grafts, anastomoses and physiological measurements are not supplied by these meshes. The source aorta and coronary trunks are orientation context only.

steps.label: Cardiac and extracardiac findings
steps.detail: Review chambers, valves, pericardium, aorta and the whole acquired field of view.
steps.look: A full field-of-view reconstruction, not only the cardiac field, in lung and soft-tissue windows.

normal.EXTRACORONARY CARDIAC FINDINGS: Cardiac chambers normal in size; pericardium normal; no significant valvular calcification; aortic root and ascending aorta normal in calibre.
normal.EXTRACARDIAC FINDINGS: No significant finding in the imaged lungs, mediastinum, upper abdomen or bones.

findings: Aortic valve calcification, [mild / moderate / severe].
Pulmonary nodule __ mm in the [lobe]; follow-up according to the applicable guideline.
Pericardial effusion, [small / moderate].
steps.anatomy_note: Only gross ventricular/atrial wall and ascending-aorta context is highlighted. Valves, pericardial layers, coronary sinuses, lungs and other acquired extracardiac anatomy are not independently represented.

steps.label: CAD-RADS 2.0
steps.detail: Assign the final category, plaque burden and modifiers from the findings already recorded.
steps.look: Use the highest-grade stenosis from the segment review, the burden step and each applicable modifier (N, HRP, I, S, G, E).
steps.normal: Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS 0.
findings: Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS __/P__ [/HRP] [/S] [/G] [/I+ / I− / I±] [/E].
Final CAD-RADS: CAD-RADS N — non-diagnostic; obstructive disease cannot be excluded.
steps.tip: The category follows the highest-grade stenosis; when reliable burden methods disagree, use the most severe.
steps.anatomy_note: The atlas supplies anatomical orientation only. CAD-RADS, plaque burden, diagnostic quality and physiology must follow acquired evidence; a mesh selection cannot establish the classification.

steps.label: Ventricular volumes and function
steps.detail: Quantify both ventricles from the short-axis cine stack.
steps.look: Short-axis cine from base to apex; contour end diastole and end systole; compare with sex- and age-specific references.
steps.normal: Normal biventricular size and systolic function: LVEDVi __ mL/m², LVEF __%; RVEDVi __ mL/m², RVEF __%.
findings: Dilated left ventricle (LVEDVi __ mL/m²) with reduced ejection fraction (__%).
Right ventricular dilatation with reduced RVEF __%.

steps.label: Wall thickness and regional motion
steps.detail: Assess wall thickness, mass and regional wall motion by segment.
steps.look: Short-axis and long-axis cines; 17-segment model for motion.
steps.normal: Normal wall thickness and myocardial mass; no regional wall-motion abnormality.
findings: Asymmetric septal hypertrophy with maximal wall thickness __ mm at [basal anteroseptum].
Akinesia of the [anterior] wall in the [LAD] territory.
Apical ballooning with basal hyperkinesia (takotsubo pattern).

steps.label: Oedema and mapping
steps.detail: Review T2-weighted oedema, native T1 and T2 mapping and ECV if acquired.
steps.look: T2-weighted and mapping sequences with the local reference range and field strength.
steps.normal: No myocardial oedema; native T1 and T2 within the local reference range.
findings: Regional oedema in the [ ] segments with raised T2 (__ ms).
Diffusely raised native T1 (__ ms) and ECV (__%).
steps.tip: Mapping values depend on scanner and sequence; always quote the local reference range.

steps.label: Late gadolinium enhancement
steps.detail: Map LGE by segment, layer, transmurality and coronary territory.
steps.look: Short- and long-axis LGE in matching planes; check the myocardium is correctly nulled.
steps.normal: No late gadolinium enhancement.
findings: Subendocardial / transmural LGE in the [LAD] territory, __% transmural (ischaemic pattern).
Midwall LGE in the septum (non-ischaemic pattern).
Subepicardial LGE in the inferolateral wall (myocarditis pattern).
Patchy LGE at the RV insertion points in hypertrophied segments (HCM pattern).
steps.tip: Ischaemic scar always involves the subendocardium; midwall or subepicardial LGE indicates a non-ischaemic cause.

steps.label: Atria, valves, thrombus and pericardium
steps.detail: Inspect the atria, valves, thrombus, pericardium and extracardiac findings.
steps.look: Long-axis cines and early post-contrast images for thrombus.
steps.normal: Atria normal; no valvular abnormality; no thrombus; pericardium normal.
findings: Left ventricular apical thrombus __ mm (non-enhancing on early post-contrast images).
Pericardial effusion __ mm.
Mitral regurgitation jet on cine.
steps.tip: An apical thrombus after anterior infarction is best seen as a non-enhancing filling defect on early post-contrast images.

steps.label: Extent and Stanford type
steps.detail: Identify actual proximal/distal disease extent and ascending/root involvement. Name the classification framework; retain arch-only or atypical patterns anatomically.
steps.look: Unenhanced and arterial phase images from the root to the iliacs; sagittal oblique reformats.
steps.normal: Aortic extent assessment: [adequate actual coverage/reconstruction / limited / unassessed]. Source-observed disease and proximal/distal limits: [ ]. Ascending/root involvement and unresolved extent: [ ].
findings: Stanford type A: involves the ascending aorta from the [root] to the [ ].
Classic Stanford type B: ascending aorta is not involved. Actual proximal/distal extent and tear site [ ]; arch involvement and any named non-A/non-B framework [ ].
steps.tip: Classic Stanford classification is based on ascending-aortic involvement, irrespective of tear origin. Describe arch-only/atypical patterns and the named framework explicitly; immediately communicate suspected acute aortic syndrome, rupture or malperfusion.

steps.label: Dissection, intramural haematoma or ulcer
steps.detail: Distinguish dissection with a flap from intramural haematoma and penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer.
steps.look: Unenhanced images for crescentic hyperattenuating wall thickening; contrast images for flap, lumina and ulceration.
findings: Intimal flap from [ ] to [ ]; source-supported lumen identity/supply [ ] and actual beak/cobweb or continuity findings [ ].
Intramural haemorrhagic wall thickening at [ ], __ mm in the stated plane; classic flap [seen / not seen / unresolved], focal tear/ULP evidence and limits [ ].
Penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer of the [descending aorta], __ mm deep and __ mm wide.
steps.tip: Beak/cobweb morphology and continuity with undissected aorta can support lumen identification. Confirm actual source course, enhancement phase and thrombus; lumen size alone is not definitive, and IMH, tiny tears or ulcerative features may overlap.

steps.label: Branches and malperfusion
steps.detail: Describe branch involvement, true or false lumen supply and organ perfusion.
steps.look: Coronary ostia, supra-aortic, coeliac, SMA, renal and iliac arteries; organ enhancement.
steps.normal: Branch/perfusion assessment: [adequate actual phases and coverage / limited / unassessed]. Each branch, side, observed lumen supply/patency and organ enhancement finding: [ ]. Unresolved supply, mechanism or uncovered territory: [ ].
findings: Dissection extends into the [brachiocephalic / left common carotid] artery.
Left renal artery arises from the false lumen with a reduced left nephrogram.
SMA compromised with poorly enhancing bowel (malperfusion).
steps.tip: Branch extension and ostial compromise can suggest static or dynamic mechanisms, but a static snapshot does not prove time-varying obstruction. Correlate actual perfusion findings and clinical evidence; branch involvement alone does not establish malperfusion syndrome.

steps.label: Rupture and complications
steps.detail: Look for rupture, pericardial blood, mediastinal and pleural haemorrhage.
steps.look: Pericardium, mediastinum and pleural spaces; periaortic haematoma.
steps.normal: Complication assessment: [adequate actual source/coverage / limited / unassessed]. Observed leak, haemorrhage compartments, pericardial/pleural findings and unresolved extent: [ ]. Clinical/echocardiographic haemodynamic correlation if indicated: [ ].
findings: Pericardial blood/effusion at [ ], with urgent clinical/echocardiographic assessment for possible haemodynamic compromise; tamponade is not diagnosed from volume alone.
Mediastinal haematoma and [left] haemothorax, compatible with rupture.

steps.label: Diameters and prior repair
steps.detail: Record aortic diameters at standard levels and any prior repair.
steps.look: Measure perpendicular to the centreline at the sinuses, ascending aorta, arch and descending aorta.
findings: Maximum diameters: sinuses __ mm, ascending __ mm, arch __ mm, descending __ mm.
Previous [ascending graft / TEVAR] with [ ].
steps.tip: Pulsation artefact in the ascending aorta can mimic a flap; check for the same line outside the aortic wall.

steps.label: Annulus
steps.detail: Record the annular area, perimeter and minimum and maximum diameters on the systolic plane.
steps.look: Define the actual annular basal plane from source-resolved cusp attachment landmarks, retaining bicuspid/other morphology. Use the appropriate available systolic reconstruction, record the exact phase/quality, and retain limits if the optimal phase is unavailable.
findings: Annulus at __% phase: area __ mm², perimeter __ mm, diameters __ × __ mm.
steps.tip: Record area, perimeter and both diameters from an actual defined plane; retain cardiac phase, edge/calibration and source limits. Prosthesis sizing is device-specific heart-team planning, not a single diameter or generic model result.

steps.label: Valve and left ventricular outflow tract
steps.detail: Describe cusp morphology, raphe, leaflet calcium and LVOT calcium.
steps.look: Short-axis view of the valve in systole and diastole; calcium distribution on the non-contrast and contrast images.
findings: Actual valve morphology [ ]; leaflet/LVOT calcium location and extent [ ]. Calcium score [performed on named protocol / not performed / unavailable]; actual score/method [ ].
Bicuspid valve with a [calcified] raphe between the [ ] cusps.
Bulky LVOT calcium at [ ], extent [ ]; relation to annulus, neighbouring structures and proposed procedure [ ], with device/clinical planning limits [ ].
steps.tip: Qualitative calcium on contrast CT is not an automatically valid Agatston score. Record the actual scoring acquisition/method and clinical context; calcification alone does not establish functional stenosis or a complication.

steps.label: Coronary heights and obstruction risk
steps.detail: Measure the ostial heights and relate the leaflets and sinuses to the coronary ostia.
steps.look: Measure each ostium from the defined annular basal plane to its inferior margin; preserve side, sinus/leaflet geometry, coronary origin/course and any prior valve/graft. Retain unavailable coronary/device relations.
findings: Left main height __ mm; right coronary height __ mm.
Low coronary height with a narrow sinus and bulky leaflet: coronary obstruction risk.
steps.tip: Coronary height alone does not determine obstruction risk. Include actual leaflet/cusp geometry, sinus/STJ dimensions, calcium and prior valve/device relationships; any virtual-device distances require explicit simulation assumptions and source-based heart-team review.

steps.label: Aortic root and ascending aorta
steps.detail: Measure the sinuses, sinotubular junction and ascending aorta and describe angulation.
steps.look: Perpendicular measurements; aortic root angulation relative to the horizontal plane.
findings: Sinus of Valsalva __ mm; sinotubular junction __ mm at __ mm height; ascending aorta __ mm.
Horizontal aorta with root angulation of __°.
steps.tip: Record actual sinus-specific dimensions, STJ height/diameter and ascending/root angulation with named plane, phase and convention. Static morphology or a generic model does not establish device suitability.

steps.label: Access routes
steps.detail: Assess minimal luminal diameters, calcification and tortuosity along each iliofemoral route.
steps.look: Curved reconstructions of the aorta, iliac and common femoral arteries on both sides.
findings: Right iliofemoral minimum lumen __ × __ mm at the [external iliac]; left __ × __ mm.
Circumferential calcification and severe tortuosity of the [ ] external iliac artery.
Actual candidate alternative route [ ], source coverage [ ], limiting segments/interfaces [ ]; suitability and device/clinical planning constraints [ ].
steps.tip: Trace each actual candidate route by side; name minimum inner lumen, location, orthogonal method, calcium and tortuosity. Sheath/device requirements and complete route coverage matter; no universal diameter cutoff or automatic access recommendation is derived from a generic model.

model.reporting_aim: Orient the arch region while inspecting actual source images for every anomalous vessel, airway and oesophageal relation. This generic aorta model does not contain the actual anomaly, pulmonary/systemic venous tree, ductal/ligamentous ring or complete airway anatomy.

steps.label: Aortic arch
steps.detail: Establish arch side, branching order, aberrant subclavian artery, diverticulum, double arch and coarctation.
steps.look: Axial images above the arch for the four-artery sign; volume rendering of the arch and branches.
findings: Right aortic arch with aberrant left subclavian artery arising from a Kommerell diverticulum (__ mm).
Left arch with aberrant right subclavian artery passing behind the oesophagus.
Double aortic arch with a dominant [right] arch.
Coarctation distal to the left subclavian artery, minimum diameter __ mm, with collaterals.
steps.tip: Describe each patent or inferred atretic component and ductal/ligamentous attachment. The four-artery sign and flat volume rendering do not independently prove all ring components or the actual anomaly geometry.

steps.label: Airway and oesophagus
steps.detail: Look for a vascular ring or sling compressing the trachea or oesophagus.
steps.look: Minimum-intensity projections of the trachea; oesophagus behind the arch.
findings: Tracheal narrowing to __ mm at the level of the [double arch / innominate artery].
Posterior oesophageal impression by the aberrant subclavian artery.
steps.tip: Record respiratory phase and actual level/length of narrowing. Static narrowing alone does not diagnose dynamic tracheobronchomalacia; cartilage and bronchial anomalies require source-resolved assessment.

steps.label: Pulmonary arteries
steps.detail: Assess the pulmonary artery origin and course, agenesis, sling and patent ductus.
steps.look: Axial and coronal images of the main and branch pulmonary arteries.
findings: Left pulmonary artery arises from the right pulmonary artery and passes between the trachea and oesophagus (pulmonary sling).
Unilateral pulmonary artery [agenesis / hypoplasia].
Patent ductus arteriosus.
steps.tip: Distinguish proximal pulmonary artery interruption from absence of lung and bronchus; trace distal arteries and systemic collateral supply. Ductal patency/flow needs adequate acquisition and appropriate functional evidence.

steps.label: Pulmonary veins
steps.detail: Trace every pulmonary vein to its drainage and look for anomalous return.
steps.look: Trace each actual lobar/segmental venous channel, common/accessory trunks, dual drainage and the complete collector route to its atrial or systemic endpoint. Record opacification and coverage limits.
findings: Partial anomalous return of the right upper-lobe vein to the superior vena cava (often with a sinus venosus defect).
Scimitar vein draining the right lung to the IVC.
Left upper-lobe vein draining via a vertical vein to the brachiocephalic vein.
steps.tip: Do not assume four separate pulmonary veins. Morphology and right-heart enlargement do not quantify shunt flow or determine haemodynamic significance. Single-phase contrast density does not independently quantify flow direction or Qp/Qs; report the actual functional source.

steps.label: Systemic veins
steps.detail: Identify a left superior vena cava, azygos continuation of the IVC and the left superior intercostal vein.
steps.look: Follow each SVC and bridging vein to its actual endpoint, assess the coronary sinus/septum and trace covered IVC/hepatic and azygos/hemiazygos connections.
findings: Persistent left superior vena cava draining into a dilated coronary sinus.
Azygos continuation of the IVC with an enlarged azygos arch.
Prominent left superior intercostal vein (aortic nipple).
steps.tip: A left SVC usually drains through the coronary sinus to the right atrium, but left-atrial drainage occurs. Do not infer its endpoint from a single left mediastinal vessel or coronary-sinus enlargement. Trace vertical/levoatriocardinal, pericardiophrenic and postoperative mimics to their actual endpoints; single-phase density is not a calibrated flow measurement.

steps.label: Device identification
steps.detail: Identify each implanted or inserted cardiovascular device.
steps.look: Whole radiograph or CT: generator, leads, valves, closure devices, stents, pumps and catheters.
findings: Dual-chamber pacemaker with right atrial and right ventricular leads.
Cardiac resynchronisation device with a coronary sinus lead.
Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with a shock coil in the right ventricle.
[Mechanical / bioprosthetic] valve in the [aortic / mitral] position.
steps.tip: Count and identify every actual component, including abandoned/retained hardware; verify model and intended configuration from records rather than generator shape alone.

steps.label: Course
steps.detail: Trace leads, catheters and conduits along their full course for kinks, fractures and abnormal routes.
steps.look: Follow each lead from the generator to the tip on frontal and lateral views.
findings: Lead fracture at the [clavicle–first rib crossing].
Twisted leads with generator rotation (Twiddler syndrome).
Lead passing through a persistent left superior vena cava.
steps.tip: Follow every component and connection, including nonstandard routes; bending/slack is device-specific and not automatically fracture or malfunction. Identify actual ECMO drainage and return routes and documented circuit type; cannula projection alone does not establish VV/VA configuration, return-jet alignment or recirculation.

steps.label: Tip and landing position
steps.detail: Assess each tip or landing zone relative to the intended anatomy.
steps.look: Use the intended device-specific site: actual atrial, ventricular, conduction-system, coronary sinus/epicardial, valve/closure/stent interface or pump/catheter route. Review balloon markers and covered branch-vessel relationships.
findings: Right ventricular lead tip projects beyond the cardiac contour, raising concern for perforation.
Balloon-pump proximal/distal markers and covered balloon/access course: [ ]; named arch/branch-vessel relationships and device-specific position uncertainty: [ ].
Coronary sinus lead in a [lateral] cardiac vein.
steps.tip: Distinguish LV-assist inflow from arterial outflow; left- and right-sided temporary pump positions differ. A projected tip or a generic arch distance does not validate complete 3D position or safety. For a dual-lumen RA-PA system, distinguish drainage and return lumens/ports using the actual model/source. ProtekDuo manufacturer describes proximal RA drainage and distal main-PA return; the source Figure 12 RV-outlet wording is not adopted as a normal target.

steps.label: Local complications
steps.detail: Review perforation, pericardial effusion, pneumothorax, haematoma and infection.
steps.look: Pericardium and pleura; generator pocket.
findings: New pericardial effusion after lead placement.
Pneumothorax after device insertion.
Pocket haematoma or collection.
steps.tip: State actual modality/coverage limits. A radiograph alone cannot exclude subtle perforation, pocket infection, effusion or physiological tamponade.

steps.label: Comparison and limits
steps.detail: Compare positions with prior imaging and state what function imaging cannot assess.
steps.look: Prior radiographs and CT.
findings: Lead retraction since [date].
Device migration of __ mm.
steps.tip: Compare actual component identity, projection, phase and source calibration. Functional performance requires appropriate interrogation/clinical imaging. Generator appearance alone does not clear MRI; specialist complete-system assessment is separate. Distinguish documented decommissioning/intentional driveline division from unplanned discontinuity. Historical HVAD recognition is not current new-implant suitability; full device-team/advisory review is separate.

model.reporting_aim: Orient the cardiac region while reviewing actual device images. This generic heart model does not contain implanted generators, leads/coils, valves/repairs, occluders, stents, pumps, cannulae, catheters or their patient-specific interfaces; device geometry and function require source-specific evidence.

steps.label: Location and attachment
steps.detail: Identify the chamber, tissue of origin, attachment and number of masses.
steps.look: Cine images to show attachment; multiplanar CT.
findings: Left atrial mass attached to the interatrial septum at the fossa ovalis (myxoma pattern).
Left atrial appendage filling defect.
Mass arising from the [ ] valve leaflet.
steps.tip: Trace actual attachment and nearby ridges, remnants, valves and vessels. Typical location is a differential clue, not automatic histology; no normality is inferred from an uncovered interface.

steps.label: Morphology
steps.detail: Describe dimensions, contour and mobility if assessed.
steps.look: Orthogonal measurements; cine for mobility and prolapse.
findings: Mass __ × __ mm with a [smooth / lobulated / villous] surface, [mobile / fixed].
Prolapse through the mitral valve in diastole.
steps.tip: Report actual measurement plane/phase. Mobility and valve prolapse require the obtained cine/echo temporal study; a still image or generic model cannot establish them.

steps.label: Tissue characteristics
steps.detail: Evaluate fat, blood, calcification and MRI signal.
steps.look: CT attenuation; MRI T1, T2 and fat-suppressed images.
findings: Fat-containing lesion of the interatrial septum sparing the fossa ovalis (lipomatous hypertrophy).
High T2 signal heterogeneous mass (myxoma pattern).
Calcified mass along the mitral annulus (caseous calcification).
steps.tip: Use actual CT/MRI sequence and reference tissues. T1/T2, fat/calcification or uptake patterns overlap; clinical/operative/pathology evidence may be required.

steps.label: Enhancement
steps.detail: Assess first-pass perfusion and late enhancement.
steps.look: First-pass perfusion and late gadolinium enhancement; long-inversion-time images for thrombus.
findings: No enhancement on the obtained adequately assessed acquisitions: [ ]. Differential confidence and unresolved organised/mixed lesion components: [ ].
Heterogeneous enhancement.
Early appendage filling defect [resolves / persists / remains uncertain] on the actual delayed acquisition; timing, quality and diagnostic confidence: [ ].
steps.tip: Thrombus usually does not enhance, but organised chronic thrombus may rarely enhance peripherally. Assess actual acquired contrast timing/sequence quality and mixed components; one phase does not establish thrombus or mixing.

steps.label: Effects and spread
steps.detail: Assess obstruction, invasion, pericardium and extracardiac disease.
steps.look: Inflow and outflow on cine; pericardium, mediastinum and lungs.
findings: Obstruction of mitral inflow.
Invasion of the myocardium and pericardium (malignant features).
Pulmonary or pleural deposits.
steps.tip: Document actual covered spread and suspicious interfaces; static appearances do not prove histology, haemodynamic obstruction or tamponade. Correlate appropriate clinical/function/staging evidence.

model.reporting_aim: Orient the cardiac region while reviewing actual lesion images. This generic heart model does not contain the actual mass, pseudomass, stalk/base, thin valvular/chordal interface, invasion, thrombus or pericardial/extracardiac disease; complete lesion geometry and function require source-specific evidence.

steps.label: Inflow
steps.detail: Assess the aorta and iliac arteries.
steps.look: First station MIP and source images of the abdominal aorta and iliac arteries.
steps.normal: Aorta and iliac arteries patent without significant stenosis.
findings: Stenosis of the [left common iliac] artery, [ ]%.
Occlusion of the [right external iliac] artery.

steps.label: Femoropopliteal segments
steps.detail: Map stenoses and occlusions by named segment and side.
steps.look: Common femoral, superficial femoral, profunda and popliteal arteries on both sides.
steps.normal: Femoral and popliteal arteries patent on both sides.
findings: Occlusion of the [right] superficial femoral artery from [ ] to [ ].
Multiple stenoses of the [left] popliteal artery.

steps.label: Lesion length and calibre
steps.detail: Describe lesion length, stenosis severity and aneurysm.
steps.look: Source images and curved reformats; measure along the vessel.
findings: Focal stenosis __ mm long.
Occlusion __ cm long.
Popliteal artery aneurysm __ mm.
steps.tip: MIP images can hide overlapping lesions or exaggerate stenosis; confirm on source images.

steps.label: Runoff and collaterals
steps.detail: Identify distal runoff and collateral reconstitution.
steps.look: Anterior tibial, posterior tibial and peroneal arteries and the pedal arch.
steps.normal: Three-vessel runoff to the foot bilaterally.
findings: [Two]-vessel runoff on the [right] via the [ ].
Reconstitution of the popliteal artery via collaterals.

steps.label: Technical limitations
steps.detail: Identify venous contamination, bolus timing problems, motion and metal artefacts.
steps.look: Lower-leg station for venous overlap; stents for susceptibility artefact.
steps.normal: Diagnostic arterial opacification throughout; no significant artefact.
findings: Venous contamination in the calf limits runoff assessment.
Stent artefact in the [ ] prevents lumen assessment.

steps.label: Cardiac chambers
steps.detail: Follow the flow of blood through the chambers and review their size and structure.
steps.look: Go with the flow: venae cavae, right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, left atrium, left ventricle and aorta.
steps.normal: Cardiac chambers normal in size.
findings: Right ventricular dilatation with contrast reflux into the IVC and hepatic veins.
Left atrial enlargement.
Left atrial appendage filling defect (thrombus versus mixing).
steps.tip: Following the direction of blood flow is a systematic way to review the heart on any chest CT.

steps.label: Myocardium
steps.detail: Assess myocardial thickness, fat and calcification.
steps.look: Left ventricular wall on soft-tissue windows.
steps.normal: Myocardium normal.
findings: Subendocardial fat or calcification in the [ ] wall (old infarction).
Left ventricular aneurysm at the apex.
Left ventricular hypertrophy.

steps.label: Coronary and valve calcification
steps.detail: Report visible coronary and valve calcification within the limits of a non-gated scan.
steps.look: Coronary arteries and aortic and mitral valves.
steps.normal: No coronary or valve calcification.
findings: Coronary artery calcification [mild / moderate / severe] in the [ ].
Aortic valve calcification.
Mitral annular calcification.
steps.tip: A non-gated chest CT is not a coronary angiogram; report calcification, not stenosis.

steps.label: Great vessels and veins
steps.detail: Inspect the aorta, pulmonary arteries and major veins.
steps.look: Measure the aorta and main pulmonary artery perpendicular to their axis; trace the venae cavae.
steps.normal: Aorta and pulmonary artery normal in calibre; normal systemic veins.
findings: Dilated ascending aorta __ mm.
Main pulmonary artery __ mm, larger than the ascending aorta.
Azygos continuation of the IVC / persistent left superior vena cava.

steps.label: Pericardium
steps.detail: Assess pericardial fluid, thickening and calcification.
steps.look: The pericardium around the whole heart.
steps.normal: No pericardial effusion, thickening or calcification.
findings: Pericardial effusion __ mm.
Pericardial calcification.
Pericardial cyst at the right cardiophrenic angle.

steps.label: Opacification and evaluable level
steps.detail: Check arterial opacification, motion and mixing, and state the most distal evaluable level.
steps.look: Main pulmonary artery attenuation; review each territory on thin sections.
steps.normal: Adequate opacification; evaluable to the subsegmental level.
findings: Limited opacification: evaluable to the [segmental] level only.
Transient interruption of contrast from inspiration (mixing artefact).
steps.tip: A poorly opacified or motion-degraded segment cannot be reported as negative.

steps.label: Acute pulmonary emboli
steps.detail: Report side and most proximal level of filling defects and whether they occlude the vessel.
steps.look: Central filling defects surrounded by contrast (polo mint) or expanding the vessel.
steps.normal: No pulmonary embolism.
findings: Acute pulmonary emboli in the [right lower-lobe] arteries, most proximal at the [lobar] level.
Saddle embolus at the bifurcation.

steps.label: Chronic thromboembolic features
steps.detail: Look for webs, bands, eccentric wall-adherent material, abrupt narrowing and bronchial collaterals.
steps.look: Thin sections along each artery; mosaic perfusion on lung windows.
steps.normal: No chronic thromboembolic features.
findings: Webs and eccentric wall-adherent thrombus in the [ ] arteries (chronic).
Abrupt narrowing and pouch defects.
Enlarged bronchial arteries.
steps.tip: Chronic thrombus is eccentric and forms an obtuse angle with the wall; acute thrombus is central.

steps.label: Right heart and pulmonary artery
steps.detail: Measure RV/LV ratio, describe septal configuration and contrast reflux, and measure the main pulmonary artery.
steps.look: Axial or four-chamber reformat at the widest point of each ventricle; main pulmonary artery at the bifurcation.
steps.normal: RV/LV ratio below 1; normal septum; main pulmonary artery __ mm.
findings: RV/LV ratio __ with septal flattening and contrast reflux into the IVC (right-heart strain).
Main pulmonary artery __ mm, larger than the ascending aorta (suggests pulmonary hypertension).
steps.tip: CT signs suggest pulmonary hypertension; confirmation requires haemodynamic measurement.

steps.label: Lungs and associated causes
steps.detail: Inspect infarcts, mosaic perfusion, pleura and causes of pulmonary hypertension.
steps.look: Lung windows; left heart, congenital shunts and lung disease.
steps.normal: No infarct or mosaic perfusion; no alternative cause identified.
findings: Peripheral wedge-shaped consolidation (infarct) in the [ ].
Mosaic perfusion pattern.
Emphysema / fibrosis as a cause of pulmonary hypertension (group 3).

steps.label: Measurement method
steps.detail: Record how the aorta was measured so that the next study can repeat it.
steps.look: Check ECG gating and slice thickness, then build a centreline or double-oblique reconstruction before measuring anything.
steps.normal: Measurement method assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Non-gated CT: root measurements limited by motion.
Diameters measured on double-oblique planes perpendicular to the aortic centreline.
Maximum sinus-to-sinus [ ] mm; cardiac phase/edge convention [ ]; asymmetric dimensions [ ]; any separately named average/comparison method [ ].
steps.tip: An axial diameter of the ascending aorta is not a true cross-section; do not report it as the maximum.

steps.label: Aortic root
steps.detail: Measure the annulus, sinuses of Valsalva and sinotubular junction at their defined levels.
steps.look: Locate actual cusp attachment nadirs and the virtual basal plane using multiplanar source views. Then identify maximum sinus bulging and the sinotubular transition; preserve variant morphology and unresolved landmarks.
steps.normal: Aortic root assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Annular basal plane defined by source-resolved attachment nadirs [ ]; phase [ ]; orthogonal dimensions [ ] × [ ] mm; variant/landmark limits [ ].
Maximum sinus-to-sinus [ ] mm with edge/phase [ ]; asymmetric dimensions [ ]; separately named comparison axis/average [ ].
Sinotubular junction __ mm.
Root dilatation predominantly at the sinuses of Valsalva (__ mm).
steps.tip: Define the plane from actual attachment landmarks, not a fixed slice offset. Preserve valve/root morphology, cardiac phase, edge and asymmetric dimensions.

steps.label: Ascending aorta
steps.detail: Find the widest point between the sinotubular junction and the arch and note elongation.
steps.look: Double-oblique plane perpendicular to the centreline at the widest ascending segment; coronal and 3D views for its length.
steps.normal: Ascending aorta assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Maximal ascending aortic diameter __ mm at [level], perpendicular to the centreline.
Elongated ascending aorta; centreline length __ mm.

steps.label: Aortic arch
steps.detail: Measure the proximal and mid arch on double-oblique planes.
steps.look: Oblique sagittal view along the arch, then perpendicular planes at the proximal arch and the mid arch between the supra-aortic branch origins.
steps.normal: Aortic arch assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Proximal arch __ mm; mid arch __ mm.
Dilatation extends from the ascending aorta into the [proximal / mid] arch.

steps.label: Descending and abdominal aorta
steps.detail: Complete the remaining protocol levels.
steps.look: Perpendicular planes at the proximal descending aorta beyond the left subclavian origin, the distal descending aorta and the abdominal aorta.
steps.normal: Descending and abdominal aorta assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Proximal descending aorta __ mm; distal descending aorta __ mm.
Abdominal aorta __ mm at [level].
steps.tip: Some protocols measure the descending aorta at two levels; follow the local protocol and say which levels you used.

steps.label: Interval change
steps.detail: Compare each level with the prior study measured the same way.
steps.look: Open the prior study; if its method is unknown, remeasure it at the same levels with the current method.
steps.normal: Interval change assessment: [adequate actual source / limited / unassessed]. Observed level, source dimensions, method/phase and interpretation criteria [ ]; unavailable measurements or comparisons [ ].
findings: Increase of __ mm at [level] since [date] (__ months), measured with the same method.
Prior study was [TTE / non-gated CT / a different sinus method]; values are not directly comparable.
steps.tip: Use comparable level, phase, edge/axis/plane conventions and original source. A small numerical difference alone does not establish true growth or a universal follow-up/surgical category.
